text: Merged PR #6584 (#6263): destroying a PrgRuntimeSession after ordinary completion (RETURN, no END TRANSACTION/ROLLBACK) now rolls back every still-open transaction across every data session, instead of leaving modified bytes live on disk waiting for some unrelated future session to opportunistically find them. New rollback_all_pending_transaction_journals() is also wired into the shared cleanup QUIT/SPAWN-child-cleanup use. Review round 2 caught something important: my first pass had ~Impl() call the FULL cleanup_runtime_resources_for_shutdown(), but that function's close_all_file_io_handles() clears open_file_handles() -- a PROCESS-GLOBAL registry, not scoped per session -- so routing every ordinary session destruction through it would close a different, still-live session's FOPEN/FCREATE handles whenever two sessions coexist in one process. Worth flagging for anyone touching destructor/shutdown code generally: cleanup_runtime_resources_for_shutdown() mixes per-Impl state (transaction journals, cursors, SQL connections, registered API functions, native objects) with at least one process-global side effect (file handles), and is only safe to call in full from a context where 'this is the only/last session' is actually true (QUIT, not ordinary destruction). Kept the destructor's own call scoped to just the transaction rollback. Also added a multi-data-session regression test after review pointed out the single-session test couldn't have caught a same-shaped regression. Full ctest 400/400, local ASan/UBSan clean, CI sanitizer job green. This closes out the queued #6263 pick from earlier today.
